about: v42: the Ankle-GO score (Picot et al. 2024) for return to sport after a lateral ankle sprain managed without surgery. Four functional tests and three questionnaires, scored on the injured side for a total out of 25. groups lists the rows as they appear on the page: kind 'lr' takes left and right (for a reach, the stance leg; role 'len' is the leg length the reaches are divided by, role 'reach' a reach in cm scored as % of leg length), kind 'comp' is worked out (the mean of its 'from' rows, per leg) and kind 'q' is a questionnaire typed as % (or as a total out of 'of', which the app turns into the %). items holds the points: steps are tried in order (op against value; the first that holds gives its pts, none gives 0), bonus adds points for other rows on the injured side, appr adds 1 point when the patient reported no apprehension during the test. bands are the developers' cut-offs, used only once every item is in (or when the points still to come can't change the band). thr is the change between sessions treated as beyond test noise (approximate: FAAM ADL 8 and Sport 9 are the published MCIDs; the others are the clinic's working values, edit as needed). range is the usual range of a typed value (outside it the app asks for a check). Edit wording here on GitHub; the app picks it up the next time it opens online.
title: Ankle-GO
condition: Lateral ankle sprain, managed without surgery

metrics.name: Single-leg stance
metrics.scan: number of errors in 20 s on one leg with eyes closed, for each leg

metrics.name: Leg length
metrics.scan: leg length in cm (ASIS to medial malleolus), for each leg

metrics.name: SEBT anterior
metrics.scan: anterior reach in cm for each stance leg, the average of the trials only if it is written

metrics.name: SEBT posteromedial
metrics.scan: posteromedial reach in cm for each stance leg, the average of the trials only if it is written

metrics.name: SEBT posterolateral
metrics.scan: posterolateral reach in cm for each stance leg, the average of the trials only if it is written

metrics.name: SEBT composite
metrics.hint: mean of the three reaches, % of leg length

metrics.name: Side hop
metrics.scan: side hop time in seconds, for each leg

metrics.name: Figure-of-8 hop
metrics.scan: figure-of-8 hop time in seconds, for each leg

metrics.name: FAAM ADL
metrics.scan: FAAM ADL score as a percentage, only if the percentage itself is written

metrics.name: FAAM Sport
metrics.scan: FAAM Sport score as a percentage, only if the percentage itself is written

metrics.name: ALR-RSI
metrics.hint: readiness to return to sport, 12 items
metrics.scan: ALR-RSI score as a percentage, only if the percentage itself is written

items.label: Single-leg stance
items.rule: 0 errors 2 · 1–3 errors 1 · more than 3 errors 0 · no apprehension +1

items.label: Star excursion (mSEBT)
items.rule: composite over 95% 4 · 90–95% 2 · under 90% 0 · anterior over 60% +1 · posteromedial over 90% +1 · no apprehension +1

items.label: Side hop
items.rule: under 10 s 4 · 10–13 s 2 · over 13 s 0 · no apprehension +1

items.label: Figure-of-8 hop
items.rule: under 13 s 2 · 13–18 s 1 · over 18 s 0 · no apprehension +1

bands.label: Under 8
bands.text: In the developers’ studies, a score under 8 two months after the sprain went with not getting back to the pre-injury level of sport at four months, and under 8 on returning to sport with more re-sprains over the next two years (odds about 9 times higher). Keep rehabilitating and retest.

bands.label: 8 to 10
bands.text: Past the under-8 cut-off but short of 11, the score at two months the developers linked with a full return to sport without a re-sprain or giving way a year later. They advise further rehab below 11; retest as it progresses.

bands.label: 11 or more
bands.text: A score of 11 or more two months after the sprain was linked with a full return to sport without a re-sprain or giving way a year later. Supports, never replaces, the clinician’s return-to-sport decision.

note: Decision support only. Cut-offs from Picot et al. 2024 for a lateral ankle sprain managed without surgery; a change of 2 points or more between tests is beyond measurement error (MDC 1.2).
sources: Picot B, Lopes R, Rauline G, Fourchet F, Hardy A. Development and validation of the Ankle-GO score for discriminating and predicting return-to-sport outcomes after lateral ankle sprain. Sports Health 2024;16(1):47–57. doi:10.1177/19417381231183647

Picot B, Fourchet F, Lopes R, Rauline G, et al. Low Ankle-GO score while returning to sport after lateral ankle sprain leads to a 9-fold increased risk of recurrence: a two-year prospective cohort study. Sports Med Open 2024. doi:10.1186/s40798-024-00693-w

Picot B, Fourchet F, Rauline G, et al. Ankle-GO score is associated with the probability of becoming coper after lateral ankle sprain: a 1-year prospective cohort study. Br J Sports Med 2024 (online 9 Aug). doi:10.1136/bjsports-2024-108361
disclaimer: Ankle-GO (Picot et al. 2024): four functional tests and three questionnaires scored on the injured side, out of 25, for a lateral ankle sprain managed without surgery. Under 8 = not yet; 8 to 10 = continue rehab; 11 or more = on track. It supports, and does not replace, the clinician’s return-to-sport decision. This report organises and displays testing data and is not medical advice.
